## 1. Expansion thesis

This plan expands attention around the order in which we fail while leaving the journal row intact. Its center is two urgent columns written in an order instead of a choice. The bank tests different distances and registers for rereading the same recorded material; it does not add a new day, memory, event, relationship, quest, or system.

## 2. Story question

What does a council decide when fuel and antibiotics are both urgent and its vote can choose only an order?

## 3. Verified source record

The complete JSON entry below is copied from the current local source. Preserve its id, author_id, author_name, day, hour, knowledge_key, timestamp, and exact text. Candidate prose is editorial material, not part of the loaded row.

```json
{
  "id": "journal_raw_b3_15_general_the_order",
  "text": "Two meetings today. The Therapist at 14:00. The council at 18:00. I will write about the council because the council is the thing that will not let me sleep, and I will write about the Therapist because she is the reason I might. The Therapist knew about the quiet. I did not tell her. The Historian told her. I did not know the Historian reads the journals. I do not know if I am angry about this. I think I am not. The Historian is the bunker's memory and the memory spoke before I did, which is what memories do. The Therapist said the sessions do not have a goal and do not have an end date. I said good. I almost smiled. I did not smile. The almost is the thing I am holding onto tonight. The council was the harder meeting. Fuel at 17 days. Antibiotics at zero. We argued the order. The Electrician wants fuel first. The Surgeon wants antibiotics first. I broke it: fuel first, antibiotics second, because a dead generator makes the antibiotic run a suicide mission. The Surgeon abstained. The Priest abstained. The Priest said he could not rank fuel above medicine and could not rank medicine above fuel. I understand. I do not agree. Understanding and agreeing are different and the council needs both. I said after the vote: we are not choosing between fuel and antibiotics. We are choosing the order in which we fail at both, and hoping we do not fail at either. I do not know if that is true. I know it is the kind of thing a general says. The Hunter asked about the rifles after the meeting. He has one. I told him to carry two. He said he has one. I said I know. I did not resolve it. I do not have a second rifle. I have a vote and an order and 17 days of fuel and zero antibiotics and one rifle and 47 people who are sleeping because they do not know the number I see when I close my eyes. I will see the Therapist on Day 179. I will come because I said I would come. That is the only commitment I have made this week that I am certain I can keep. The rest is the order: fuel, then antibiotics, then whatever comes after, if anything does.",
  "timestamp": "Day 172, 23h",
  "author_name": "The General",
  "author_id": "the_general",
```

## 4. Fixed canon and open space

The council debates fuel at seventeen days and antibiotics at zero. The General orders fuel first and antibiotics second because a dead generator makes the antibiotic run a suicide mission; the Surgeon and Priest abstain. The General still has one rifle and has not resolved the Hunter’s request for a second. Do not add supply outcomes or call the order a solution. Candidate language may add an image, rhythm, or private impression as an editorial draft, but no proposed addition becomes a further remembered event or a confirmed fact until the existing content owner selects and reviews it against the source.

The source voice is The General. The General writes about two meetings, a real disagreement, and a phrase that does not make the shortage easier. Keep therapy and council distinct; preserve that he agrees the order is necessary without claiming it is correct. The prose may notice what the author can count, hear, repair, fear, or leave uncertain, while keeping the account’s limits visible.

6. **Return without closure.** Offer one last view of the anchor with no promise, new consequence, or interpretation forced on the reader. Begin or turn through journal-text excerpt 6: “not fail at either. I do not know if that is true. I know it is the kind of thing…”.
